title: Procedural snippets registry and idempotent admin helpers
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Oncall and SRE run ad-hoc scripts or copy-paste partial runbook steps for common admin flows (restarts, cache invalidation, scaling adjustments, emergency feature toggles). This causes variability, accidental double-runs, and poor telemetry. Goal: Build a lightweight "procedural snippets" registry + a small library of idempotent admin helpers that lets engineers compose verified, versioned, and auditable admin operations as first-class tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A Git-backed registry of procedural snippets where each snippet is a small, documented, versioned file (YAML + metadata)
CLI and HTTP interfaces to discover, dry-run, and execute snippets with required approvals and audit logging
Core set of 12 idempotent admin helpers (eg. safe-restart-service, kv-prefix-clear, bounded-rollout-toggle) implemented with retries and pre/post checks
Every execution emits structured telemetry (who, what, inputs, dry_run flag, result, duration) to the console events store
Integrations: compose snippets into runbook tasks consumed by the support UI and the ops-sherpa task runner
Safety guardrails: per-snippet execution limits, required approver roles, and automatic rollback hooks for defined failure classes
progress_notes: 2026-02-22: Spike completed comparing storage options (Git repo vs DB). Tradeoff: Git provides human diffability and simple code review; DB gives easier runtime mutation. Decided on Git-backed canonical store + Postgres index for search and metadata caching.

2026-02-28: Prototype CLI created (scripts/snippetctl) supporting list / show / dry-run / execute. Dry-run implemented using --dry flag that stops before side-effects; reuses runtime validation logic.

2026-03-03: Implemented first 6 idempotent helpers and added unit tests: safe-restart-service, drain-connections, bounded-toggle-flag, kv-atomic-delete, cache-prefetch, sidecar-rollout-check. All have explicit pre/post checks and idempotency tokens.

2026-03-06: Security review notes: ensure KMS usage for any credential fetch, limit network egress for snippet containers. Marked security_review_required=true for next stage. (see comment from secops)
2026-03-09: Added audit event schema and pipeline to ship events to the ops-events topic. Dashboard skeleton in Grafana created: ops-tools > snippet-executions.

2026-03-10: Started integration with ops-sherpa task runner (ENG-271443 referenced). First end-to-end: runbook UI triggers snippet execution with approver flow stubbed. Awaiting UX sign-off on confirmation modal behavior.
next_steps: Finish approver/role mapping and hook into SSO groups (estimate: 2 days)
Complete rollout test plan covering concurrent invocations and simulated partial failures
Add remaining 6 helper primitives and fuzz tests to validate idempotency under retries
UX: finalize confirmation modal copy and required justification fields for production operations
Ops-run: schedule a staged rollout to dev -> staging -> prod with feature flags
notes_for_review: Seeking feedback on the chosen event schema (see links). Events are intentionally compact (string enums + freeform metadata) to keep pipeline cost low.
Open question: should snippet inputs be schema-validated via a lightweight JSON-schema file per snippet? Current plan: yes, include optional schema metadata and enforce at runtime.
Design choice: Git as source-of-truth means merging a snippet change is the gating review step for behavior changes. Ops editors will get a small web UI tying to PRs for non-developers.
